claims.text: Droid 1.0 adds a Script tool in which the model writes JavaScript that invokes Droid tools, filters results and chains dependent operations; the JavaScript sandbox has no filesystem, network or system access of its own.
In Droid 1.0, a replay of the same 15 tool calls used five model requests with Script versus ten with direct calls, finishing in 41.6 versus 56.8 seconds.

Droid 1.0 moves concurrent sessions into a shared daemon process with approximately 20 MB incremental memory per session, versus roughly 350 MB per session before; Factory says five subagents plus the main session previously exceeded 2 GB.

Factory reports a typical production Droid request reads 98% of input from cache and 98.6% of requests are strictly append-only, because newly discovered tools are appended to the end of the request to preserve the cached prefix.
Factory estimates at least a third of summaries were filling the previous 8,000-token compaction limit, contributing to dropped tasks; Droid 1.0 raises the summary allowance to 16,000 tokens.

Factory reports that on its Terminal-Bench 4 suite, Droid with GPT-6.1 Sol scored 3.5 points above Codex at 12% lower cost but took 10% longer, and Droid with Claude Opus 5.5 used 26% less time per passed task and 17% fewer tokens than Claude Code.
Droid 1.0 loop anti-stall rules stop after three consecutive turns without visible output, nudge on three identical tool calls and stop on six, except when repeats yield new results.

Droid's OS-enforced sandbox uses macOS Seatbelt or Linux/WSL2 bubblewrap plus seccomp with a filtering proxy for outbound traffic; the default per-command mode isolates shell commands but not the main Droid process, while whole-process mode isolates Droid and spawned MCP transports and subagents.
Factory warns that sandbox-allowed domains can still provide exfiltration paths and allowed writable paths can be changed arbitrarily, and recommends containers or dedicated VMs for untrusted code.

In Factory Private, OpenCompute provisions execution sandboxes inside the customer VPC and connects outbound to Factory with no inbound firewall ports required; the control plane remains Factory-hosted by default.

droid exec defaults to read-only reconnaissance; an action exceeding its autonomy level stops the headless run with a nonzero exit, leaving earlier edits in the working tree, and exit code zero does not mean the result is correct.
Factory calls its airgapped build a cooperative reliability contract: infrastructure network isolation, not the agent, provides the actual security boundary.

Factory's August 2025 context architecture injects repository summaries, uses code-tuned vector search to rank candidate files and folder summaries, then fetches targeted files, lines, diffs and terminal output; User Memory and Org Memory persist preferences and shared conventions.
The June 2024 Code Droid report names HyperCode, a multiresolution repository representation, and ByteRank, its retrieval algorithm.

Code Droid reported 19.27% on SWE-bench Full and 31.67% first-attempt on Lite, rising to 37.67% pass@2 and 42.67% pass@6 on Lite, with typical 5-20 minutes per patch, a maximum of 136 minutes, and up to 13 million tokens per patch.
On SWE-bench Lite, Factory reported missing the target file from analysis in 8% of tasks, analyzing but not ranking it in the top five in another 8%, and prioritizing but not editing it in 6%.

Factory's July 2025 compression approach, anchored iterative summarization, summarizes newly truncated spans and merges them into a persistent rolling summary, using a high-water trigger threshold and a lower retained-context threshold.

The May 2026 Deferred Context Engine loads only names and short descriptions of tools, skills and plugins initially and promotes needed ones on demand; over five days it showed 15.1% average and 39.4% p90 input-token reduction for sessions invoking MCP tools, and 50.8% average for sessions with over 100 hidden tools.

Custom droids (subagents) are Markdown-defined agents with their own prompt, model, tools and fresh context; they return a final result to the parent and cannot ask the user directly or spawn subagents.

Missions separate an orchestrator that writes a validation contract and decomposes work, fresh-context workers that implement features in order, and validators; each milestone has scrutiny validators and user-testing validators, with failures converted into fix features.

In Factory's 16.5-hour Slack-clone Mission, 778.5 million total tokens were consumed, 38.8k lines generated with 89.25% statement coverage, validation took 37.2% of runtime, and none of six milestones passed first validation.

Mission planning documentation estimates a minimum of about features + 2 × milestones agent runs, and mission settings allow separate worker and validator models and skipping scrutiny or user-testing validation.
Factory reported 58.75% on Terminal-Bench Core v0.1.1 (80 tasks) using Claude Opus 4.1 without thinking, in September 2025.

In Factory's December 2025 compression evaluation over 36,611 messages, GPT-5.2-judged overall scores were Factory 3.70, Anthropic 3.44, OpenAI 3.35, with artifact tracking lowest at Factory 2.45, Anthropic 2.33, OpenAI 2.19 out of 5.

Independent OctoBench (January 2026, Droid v0.42.2) found Droid at 40.17% instruction success versus Claude Code 28.39% with Opus 4.5, but with MiniMax-M2.1 Droid scored 15.38% versus Claude Code's 18.60%.
